title: IPMI Sensor Threshold Violations
exclusions: Detects current threshold-class sensor conditions from a normalized IPMI poll when a valid numeric reading crosses a BMC-reported readable threshold or the current threshold state is explicitly asserted. It does not apply numeric limits to discrete sensors such as chassis intrusion, power-supply presence, redundancy, or processor-state sensors; those states require a separate discrete-event use case. It does not reconstruct historical System Event Log entries, prove that a component is physically defective, validate BMC calibration, interpret unrecognized OEM states, infer a threshold that the BMC does not expose, predict a future breach, monitor operating-system-only sensors, secure the BMC interface, change thresholds, or perform remediation. A reading/state marked unavailable is ignored as required by the IPMI sensor model. This operational monitor makes no regulatory, security-technique, or prevention claim.
evidence: After deployment, retain the versioned `ipmi_sensor_threshold_violations` saved-search definition and schedule, the effective `TA-ipmi-sensor-poll` input and JSON extraction configuration, collector source and hash, tool and BMC firmware versions recorded during qualification, raw sensor snapshots surrounding each finding, alert dispatch rows, exact suppression decision, and dated positive/negative control results. For a finding, preserve host, BMC inventory ID, sensor record ID/name/type, reading and unit, all six readable thresholds, asserted and calculated threshold states, trigger source, sample time, and severity. A same-time read from the BMC web/CLI sensor page plus `ipmi-sensors` or `ipmitool sensor get` output is corroborating evidence. These artifacts show what the polled management controller reported; this documentation-only review produced no runtime evidence and did not certify hardware health.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index, ingest a schema-1 `sourcetype=hardware:ipmi:sensor` event for `host=ipmi-positive`, `bmc_id=bmc-01`, `sensor_record_id=42`, `event_reading_class=threshold`, `collector_status=ok`, `reading_valid=1`, `reading=92`, `unit=C`, `threshold_unc=80`, `threshold_ucr=90`, `threshold_unr=100`, and `asserted_threshold=none`, with a fresh `sample_epoch`. Run the SPL with fixed bounds and expect one row whose `calculated_threshold=ucr`, `effective_threshold=ucr`, `trigger_source=numeric_comparison`, and `severity=high`. Then ingest a fresh valid event at reading 88 with the same thresholds and `asserted_threshold=ucr`; expect one high row with `trigger_source=asserted_state`, proving that the current IPMI state is retained when hysteresis makes it differ from an instantaneous comparison.
controlTest.negativeScenario: With the same fixed search bounds, require zero rows for each case independently: a threshold sensor at reading 70 with `asserted_threshold=none`; a threshold event with `reading_valid=0`; a `collector_status=command_error` event; and a discrete power-supply event with `event_reading_class=discrete`, `tool_state=critical`, `sensor_event=Power Supply AC lost`, and no numeric thresholds. Also ingest a valid lower-threshold sensor with reading 400 RPM, `threshold_lnr=200`, `threshold_lcr=500`, and `threshold_lnc=800`; confirm it produces `lcr`, not `lnr`, demonstrating the lower-side comparison order. Finally, move all samples outside the configured freshness window and confirm the alert returns zero while the independent source-health search reports stale collection.

dataSources: One normalized JSON event per sensor every 300 seconds in the deployment-selected `index=os`, `source=ipmi_sensor_snapshot`, and `sourcetype=hardware:ipmi:sensor`. The reference local, in-band collector invokes GNU FreeIPMI `ipmi-sensors` with comma-separated output, interpreted state, and six threshold columns. A separately qualified `ipmitool sensor list` adapter may emit the same contract. The contract preserves the managed `host`, stable `bmc_id`, sensor record ID/name/type, `event_reading_class`, reading validity/value/unit, LNR/LCR/LNC/UNC/UCR/UNR values, current asserted threshold state, raw sensor event, collector status, and sample epoch. Tool output is not supplied or normalized by Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux.
app: Locally managed deployment app `TA-ipmi-sensor-poll` containing the strict FreeIPMI or ipmitool adapter, scripted input, JSON source-type configuration, source-health searches, saved search, and dashboard. It uses the Splunk Universal Forwarder's native scripted-input capability; no Splunkbase or premium app is required. The reference script is local in-band only. A central out-of-band collector requires a separately reviewed target inventory and credential mechanism while preserving the same event contract.

| fields _time host bmc_id collector_schema collector_status sample_epoch event_reading_class reading_valid sensor_record_id sensor_name sensor_type reading unit threshold_lnr threshold_lcr threshold_lnc threshold_unc threshold_ucr threshold_unr asserted_threshold sensor_event tool_state
| eval collector_schema=tonumber(collector_schema), sample_epoch=tonumber(sample_epoch), reading_valid=tonumber(reading_valid), reading=tonumber(reading), threshold_lnr=tonumber(threshold_lnr), threshold_lcr=tonumber(threshold_lcr), threshold_lnc=tonumber(threshold_lnc), threshold_unc=tonumber(threshold_unc), threshold_ucr=tonumber(threshold_ucr), threshold_unr=tonumber(threshold_unr), asserted_threshold=lower(asserted_threshold)
| where collector_schema=1 AND collector_status="ok" AND event_reading_class="threshold" AND reading_valid=1 AND isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(bmc_id) AND isnotnull(sensor_record_id) AND isnotnull(reading) AND sample_epoch>0
| eval sample_age_seconds=now()-sample_epoch
| where sample_age_seconds>=0 AND sample_age_seconds<=660

| eval calculated_threshold=case(isnotnull(threshold_lnr) AND reading<=threshold_lnr,"lnr",isnotnull(threshold_unr) AND reading>=threshold_unr,"unr",isnotnull(threshold_lcr) AND reading<=threshold_lcr,"lcr",isnotnull(threshold_ucr) AND reading>=threshold_ucr,"ucr",isnotnull(threshold_lnc) AND reading<=threshold_lnc,"lnc",isnotnull(threshold_unc) AND reading>=threshold_unc,"unc",true(),"none")

description: Finds current IPMI threshold-class sensor breaches by comparing each valid numeric reading with the six readable limits reported by the management controller and by preserving an explicitly asserted current threshold state. It keeps lower and upper non-critical, critical, and non-recoverable conditions distinct, while excluding discrete sensor assertions from numeric comparison.
value: Temperature, voltage, current, fan, and power readings can leave their platform-defined operating ranges before the host operating system supplies a useful symptom. Accurate out-of-band threshold evidence helps hardware and data-center responders detect the affected sensor and direction early, preserve the reading, unit, and BMC limit, and avoid flattening every condition into an ambiguous generic warning or misclassifying a discrete component state.
implementation: Deploy the local read-only collector through `TA-ipmi-sensor-poll`, poll every five minutes, and emit the documented schema-1 JSON contract. Use the BMC's readable LNR/LCR/LNC/UNC/UCR/UNR values rather than catalogue-wide temperature or voltage constants. Preserve current asserted threshold state separately from the instantaneous numeric comparison, reject unavailable readings, and route discrete assertions to a separate monitor. Schedule the saved search every five minutes over a delayed closed window, test both high- and low-going conditions, and maintain independent alerts for collector errors, stale targets, parse failures, and inventory gaps.
visualization: Use a latest-state table with host, BMC ID, sensor name/type, severity, exact threshold code and direction, trigger source, reading, unit, applicable threshold, asserted state, calculated state, raw event, and sample age. Add separate 24-hour timecharts for numeric reading and the readable thresholds by one selected sensor, plus tiles for breached sensors, stale BMC targets, command/parse errors, unavailable readings, and discrete or unknown-class events excluded from this search. Never combine unlike units on one axis, turn a missing threshold into zero, or label an interpreted discrete state as a numeric threshold breach.
dataModelAcceleration: No documented CIM dataset represents IPMI SDR record identity, event/reading class, reading-validity state, all six BMC sensor thresholds, or current discrete assertion bits. Use the local raw-event contract. No accelerated `tstats` equivalent is claimed.

knownFalsePositives:
Every result should represent either a current threshold state reported by the BMC or a valid reading beyond a readable BMC threshold under this event contract. It can still be expected, misleading, or non-actionable for notification policy.

1. **Approved thermal or power test** — Burn-in, fan-failover, power-supply, chamber, and resilience tests can deliberately cross a threshold. Confirm the exact host, sensor record, test owner, safety plan, and bounded UTC window. Preserve findings as control evidence even when notifications are suppressed.

2. **Workload transition or environmental excursion** — Boot, firmware initialization, dense batch work, fan spin-up, or a short facilities temperature change can produce a real non-critical crossing that self-clears. Compare duration, adjacent sensors, workload/change records, and the BMC's current page; do not call the reading false merely because the hardware recovered.

3. **BMC threshold or calibration defect** — Firmware can expose duplicated, implausible, disabled, or platform-inappropriate limits, and a sensor can drift. The SPL correctly compares the supplied values but cannot validate them. Compare vendor platform documentation, BMC UI, firmware release notes, and a trusted physical measurement before changing a threshold.

4. **Hysteresis or sampling boundary** — The asserted IPMI threshold state can remain active after the instantaneous reading moves back inside its nominal boundary, or a poll can catch a reading beyond a threshold before the state changes. The result keeps both values and labels the trigger source; investigate the disagreement instead of discarding one field.

5. **Sensor identity changed after service or firmware update** — SDR record IDs and names can be reordered, duplicated, or renamed. A stale inventory mapping can route the right condition to the wrong component owner. Reconcile record ID, sensor number, entity, FRU, BMC firmware, and current inventory after hardware or firmware work.

6. **OEM interpretation or parser mismatch** — Unrecognized OEM output, localization, a changed column layout, or a permissive parser can create incorrect fields. The reference adapter forces the C locale and rejects the wrong column count, but it is still a qualification sample. Treat parse errors and unknown classes as source-health failures, not normal sensors.

7. **Duplicate collectors or delayed forwarding** — Two stanzas polling one BMC or a queue releasing old events can make a cleared state appear current. The search deduplicates on the newest sample and enforces sample age, but duplicate collection must be removed and late data retained for diagnosis.

**Safe suppression:** keep the catalogue SPL unchanged and apply a post-result lookup named `ipmi_sensor_threshold_exceptions.csv` only in the deployed alert wrapper. Key it on exact `host`, `bmc_id`, and `sensor_record_id`; require `valid_from_epoch`, `valid_until_epoch`, `owner`, `ticket`, `reason`, and `approver`; reject wildcards and non-expiring entries. Preserve suppressed rows in a review panel. Never suppress command/parse errors, stale collection, unavailable-reading trends, all sensors on a host, or non-recoverable states merely because a non-critical state is expected.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational BMC sensor-threshold monitoring; no adversary behavior or intent is asserted)

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and semantic boundary

Assign a hardware-platform owner, BMC access owner, Splunk data owner, and alert-response owner. Use an IPMI-capable management controller whose Sensor Data Repository can be read through a supported in-band interface. The reference adapter is designed for a local Linux Universal Forwarder and GNU FreeIPMI `ipmi-sensors`; it does not include remote credentials. Grant the forwarder service account only the device access needed by the selected IPMI driver. Test that account directly. Do not grant unrestricted `sudo`, BMC administrator rights, threshold-write permission, chassis power control, or access to remote-console functions merely to read sensors.

Treat IPMI semantics precisely. The specification allows an analog or discrete reading and a threshold-based or discrete event type; those axes are not interchangeable. Threshold sensors can expose up to six readable limits: lower non-recoverable (`lnr`), lower critical (`lcr`), lower non-critical (`lnc`), upper non-critical (`unc`), upper critical (`ucr`), and upper non-recoverable (`unr`). Discrete sensors report active states or assertion bits, not a numeric value to compare with those six limits. A power-supply presence assertion marked critical by an interpretation file is therefore not an 0-value threshold breach. Keep it in the raw feed and route it to a separate discrete-state search.

The IPMI Get Sensor Reading response also has a reading/state-unavailable indication. When it is set, software must ignore the reading/state. In this contract, a nonnumeric or unavailable reading produces `reading_valid=0`, and the detection excludes it even if stale text appears severe. Alert independently on unavailable-reading prevalence because loss of observability is important but is not proof of a threshold breach.

Current threshold assertion and instantaneous numeric comparison can disagree legitimately because of hysteresis, polling time, event enablement, or BMC implementation. Preserve both. The collector's canonical `asserted_threshold` records a recognized current threshold event; the SPL calculates a second state from the current reading and readable limits. Neither is overwritten by FreeIPMI's configurable `NOMINAL`, `WARNING`, or `CRITICAL` interpretation. `tool_state` remains context only because FreeIPMI documents that its state is derived from `freeipmi_interpret_sensor.conf`, and default policy can classify some non-critical threshold events differently from local paging policy.

## Step 1a — Qualify the tool output and sensor inventory

Install a maintained distribution package for GNU FreeIPMI or ipmitool on canary hosts. Record the exact package version, BMC model, BMC firmware, system product, access driver, and qualification date in deployment inventory; this review does not assert a minimum safe version. Run the command as the forwarder account with `LC_ALL=C`:

```bash
/usr/sbin/ipmi-sensors --comma-separated-output --output-sensor-state --output-sensor-thresholds --entity-sensor-names
```

FreeIPMI documents that its default record contains record ID, sensor name, sensor type, reading, and current event; the selected options add interpreted state and all six thresholds. On the qualified output, verify the header order before enabling `--no-header-output`: record ID, name, type, interpreted state, reading, unit, LNR, LCR, LNC, UNC, UCR, UNR, event. The reference script expects exactly those 13 columns and emits `parse_error` otherwise. It uses Python's CSV parser rather than splitting on commas. Keep `--entity-sensor-names` stable after qualification because it can disambiguate repeated labels. Do not enable `--interpret-oem-data` by default: FreeIPMI warns that OEM interpretation correctness cannot be guaranteed across vendor changes. If a platform requires it, qualify every relevant state and document that dependency.

Build an inventory from the BMC's sensor page and both raw tool views. Classify each sensor as threshold, discrete, or unknown; capture record ID, sensor number where available, entity/FRU association, expected unit, readable thresholds, and owner. Threshold values of `N/A` mean unavailable, not zero. Duplicate numeric thresholds can be legitimate but deserve vendor review. An analog reading with no readable threshold remains `unknown` under the conservative reference adapter and is not alertable until the event/reading type is obtained and normalized safely.

ipmitool is an acceptable alternate adapter, not an interchangeable text substitution. Upstream `ipmitool sensor list` prints a wide table and its default status can collapse direction to `nc`, `cr`, or `nr`; the upstream implementation can also expose directional forms such as `lnr` and `ucr` in extended output. If using ipmitool, parse a pinned, canary-tested format, preserve all six threshold columns, and derive direction only from a recognized directional state or numeric comparison. Never translate generic `cr` into upper critical without checking the reading against available lower and upper limits. Use `ipmitool sensor get "<name>"` and `sdr` detail during validation, not a hard-coded column guess.

## Step 1b — Configure data collection and the source type

Place the reviewed adapter at `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA-ipmi-sensor-poll/bin/collect_ipmi_sensors.py`. The `scriptExample` is a transparent qualification baseline, not a claim of production validation. It invokes no shell, forces the C locale, enforces a 45-second timeout, emits one compact JSON object per sensor, and emits explicit `command_error` or `parse_error` events instead of fabricating healthy values. Review `platform.node()` as the local `bmc_id`; replace it with a governed stable asset identifier if hostnames can change. Keep secrets out of source, arguments, stdout, stderr-derived fields, and Splunk configuration.

Create `local/inputs.conf`:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA-ipmi-sensor-poll/bin/collect_ipmi_sensors.py]
disabled = 0
interval = 300
index = os
source = ipmi_sensor_snapshot
sourcetype = hardware:ipmi:sensor
```

Splunk documents numeric scripted-input intervals in seconds and schedules from script completion, so 300 seconds is a target cadence rather than a real-time guarantee. Each successful poll emits one event per returned sensor; a BMC exposing 80 sensors produces about 23,040 small events per day. That is arithmetic from the configured cadence, not a license-size estimate. Measure serialized bytes, execution time, device contention, and forwarding delay on canaries before fleet deployment. Avoid overlapping a second hardware-management poller if the BMC or in-band driver cannot handle concurrent access reliably.

Configure line breaking, epoch event time, and search-time JSON extraction on the appropriate parsing/search tiers:

```ini
[hardware:ipmi:sensor]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = ([\r\n]+)
TRUNCATE = 0
TIME_PREFIX = "sample_epoch"\s*:\s*
TIME_FORMAT = %s
MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD = 10
KV_MODE = json
```

Do not combine `KV_MODE=json` with `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=JSON` for the same events. Confirm the winning stanza with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` and inspect forwarder `ExecProcessor` messages. Maintain a separate source-health search for missing hosts/BMC IDs, newest `sample_epoch`, non-`ok` collector statuses, parse-error count, unavailable-reading rate, and the inventory difference between expected and observed sensor record IDs. Absence of a threshold finding is never evidence that collection is healthy.

For a central out-of-band design, do not reuse this local script unchanged. Define an allow-listed target inventory mapping BMC endpoint to managed `host` and stable `bmc_id`; use a secret store or tool-supported protected credential source; require encrypted IPMI 2.0 transport where platform support and policy allow; bound timeouts and concurrency; and emit one explicit target-level error when authentication, transport, or SDR retrieval fails. Never index passwords, privilege keys, session material, full command lines, or unrestricted BMC addresses. Qualify that design independently because remote transport, bridging, privilege, and cache behavior differ from local in-band access.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the saved search

Save the catalogue SPL as `ipmi_sensor_threshold_violations`. Schedule it every five minutes after measuring ingestion delay. Its base range reads from 12 minutes through one minute before dispatch, selects the newest qualified event per exact `host`, `bmc_id`, and `sensor_record_id`, and rejects samples older than 660 seconds. The delayed end avoids racing the current poll; the broad start tolerates one missed five-minute poll. Tune these windows from `_indextime-_time` observations, but keep a stricter independent stale-source alert.

The first `where` is the semantic firewall: schema 1, successful collection, threshold class, valid numeric reading, stable identity, and positive sample epoch are mandatory. Discrete and unknown classes cannot reach numeric comparison even if `tool_state=critical`. Numeric casting prevents lexical errors such as treating `9` as greater than `100`.

The comparison order matters. On the lower side, the search tests LNR before LCR before LNC; on the upper side, UNR before UCR before UNC. It interleaves severity so the most severe crossed readable boundary wins. Missing limits remain null and are skipped. Equality counts as a crossing because the IPMI state definitions are at-or-below or at-or-above. These values come from the current BMC/SDR snapshot; the catalogue supplies no universal Celsius, volt, ampere, watt, or RPM threshold.

`asserted_rank` and `calculated_rank` retain two independent signals. Non-recoverable maps to rank 3, critical to rank 2, and non-critical to rank 1. The higher rank becomes `effective_threshold`; ties prefer the explicit asserted direction. `trigger_source` states whether assertion, numeric comparison, or both produced the row. Routing severity is a local alert vocabulary: rank 3 is `critical`, rank 2 `high`, and rank 1 `warning`. It does not rename IPMI's exact threshold state, and it does not claim that “non-recoverable” proves irreversible damage.

Trigger when result count is greater than zero. Use per-result notification and suppress repeated actions on exact `host,bmc_id,sensor_record_id` for one poll interval while retaining every scheduled result. Splunk's saved-search reference documents field-based suppression; verify deployed ownership and digest mode because suppression behavior depends on alert configuration. Do not suppress source-health searches with the threshold alert.

## Step 3 — Validate semantics, fields, freshness, and controls

On each canary platform, compare one same-time poll with the BMC's hardware-health or sensor page and with `ipmi-sensors` output. For two known threshold sensors, verify record identity, name/type, reading, unit, all available thresholds, and current event. For two discrete sensors, verify that the raw event or active states are retained but `event_reading_class=discrete` and numeric threshold fields remain null. For unavailable and OEM sensors, verify conservative `reading_valid=0` or `event_reading_class=unknown`; never edit the parser merely to make every row alertable.

Run `ipmitool sensor get "<sensor name>"` as an independent tool comparison when supported. Account for adjacent sampling time and display rounding. A small numeric difference does not automatically indicate a parser defect; a changed unit, threshold direction, record identity, or order does. Confirm that lower limits normally preserve their actual ordering and that the search still chooses the most severe crossed limit when vendor data duplicates or omits values.

Execute every `controlTest` case in an isolated index with absolute earliest/latest bounds. Inspect intermediate fields before the final table. The 92 C event must choose UCR rather than UNC; the 400 RPM event must choose LCR rather than LNC or LNR. The asserted-UCR event below UCR must remain visible with `trigger_source=asserted_state`, documenting possible hysteresis. The discrete critical event, unavailable reading, command error, and safe threshold event must produce no threshold row. Then prove source-health logic independently sees command errors and stale targets.

Check completeness over at least one day: count events per poll bucket and BMC ID; compare distinct observed record IDs with inventory; list every collector status, class, tool state, unit, and null threshold pattern; and calculate p95/max ingest delay. Reboot a canary and restart its BMC only under an approved procedure, then verify recovery without duplicate stanzas or stale cache. Repeat qualification after BMC firmware, system firmware, motherboard, sensor/FRU, FreeIPMI/ipmitool, operating system, forwarder, adapter, or parsing changes.

This review did not run the adapter against a BMC, ingest fixtures, execute the SPL in Splunk, or validate a Splunk platform version. Keep `status=draft` until the positive and negative controls, platform matrix, security review, and hardware SME review are complete.

## Step 4 — Operationalize triage, evidence, and safe suppression

Build the visualization exactly around threshold semantics. Show the exact code and direction, not only color. A responder must be able to distinguish low fan RPM from high temperature and upper voltage from lower voltage. Keep units beside every value and prevent panels from plotting heterogeneous sensors on one scale. Put collection-health tiles above the breach table so an empty table cannot be mistaken for a healthy fleet.

The response runbook should: (1) confirm a fresh successful raw event and stable sensor identity; (2) compare the current BMC page plus a new read from the qualified tool; (3) inspect adjacent sensors sharing the entity or FRU, such as inlet and CPU temperatures or redundant fan/power channels; (4) check workload, maintenance, firmware, facilities, and environmental changes; (5) determine whether asserted and calculated states agree and whether hysteresis explains a difference; (6) consult model-specific vendor service documentation for the exact sensor and threshold; and (7) escalate physical inspection, workload reduction, failover, or shutdown to authorized hardware/facilities owners. Splunk must not automatically write thresholds, issue raw IPMI commands, power-cycle chassis, alter fan policy, acknowledge hardware alarms, or execute values from result fields.

Retain the artifacts listed in `evidence` according to local operational and incident policy. BMC endpoints and hardware inventory can be sensitive; restrict raw searches, dashboard drilldowns, and exports to appropriate operations roles. The evidence contract does not claim a universal retention period or an audit index. Apply only exact, expiring post-result suppressions described in `knownFalsePositives`, review them at least at expiry, and continue retaining suppressed matches and source-health results.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting without inventing state

- **No events:** run the adapter as the forwarder account, verify the FreeIPMI executable path and in-band driver/device permission, inspect effective `inputs.conf`, and review `ExecProcessor` messages. Do not solve device denial with blanket root access.
- **`command_error`:** execute the exact command with the same account and locale; check driver availability, BMC responsiveness, concurrent pollers, timeout, and firmware state. The wrapper intentionally does not index stderr because tool errors can disclose connection details.
- **`parse_error`:** run once with headers, compare the 13-column qualified layout, package version, locale, CSV quoting, and selected options. Do not silently shift columns or coerce extra text into readings.
- **Many `unknown` classes:** inspect event/reading type and SDR detail with verbose FreeIPMI or ipmitool output. Add a platform-specific classification only after proving it across normal, asserted, unavailable, and OEM cases.
- **Critical discrete sensor missing from this alert:** this is expected. Use a discrete-state rule over `event_reading_class=discrete` and `active_states`; never add `OR tool_state=critical` to the threshold SPL.
- **Reading visible but `reading_valid=0`:** check whether the text includes a unit or unsupported formatting, or whether the tool returned N/A/Unknown. Update a tested parser for the exact format; do not strip arbitrary characters until a number appears.
- **Asserted and calculated states disagree:** compare timestamps, hysteresis behavior, event enablement, readable thresholds, BMC UI, and another immediate poll. Keep both signals. Do not force the asserted state to match the arithmetic.
- **Wrong lower-threshold severity:** verify the vendor's LNR/LCR/LNC values and that numeric fields are not swapped. The search deliberately tests the most severe lower boundary first.
- **Thresholds appear as zero:** inspect the raw event and adapter. N/A must become null. A real zero can be valid for some sensor types, so do not globally discard it; qualify against the BMC and unit.
- **Repeated old finding:** compare `sample_epoch`, `_time`, `_indextime`, app assignment, and duplicate stanzas. The 660-second age gate excludes old samples from notification but does not repair collection.
- **Sensor disappeared after service:** compare SDR inventory, record IDs, entity/FRU association, BMC reset history, and firmware. Update the governed inventory and retest; do not reuse an old ID for a new component silently.

Revalidate the collector, field contract, controls, thresholds, owner routing, and safe suppression after every material change. A parser that continues producing JSON is not enough; it must continue preserving the IPMI distinction between valid threshold readings and discrete states.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the server's built-in temperature, fan, voltage, and power gauges against the safe limits reported by the hardware. If a valid reading crosses one of those limits, the team sees exactly which gauge moved and how serious the hardware says it is.
hardware: An IPMI-capable baseboard management controller with readable Sensor Data Records and an in-band interface accessible to the local collector. Remote BMC collection is possible only through a separately qualified credential and target-inventory design.
scriptExample:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reference local FreeIPMI adapter for UC-1.1.103; qualify before production."""
import csv
import json
import math
import os
import platform
import subprocess
import time

COMMAND = [
    "/usr/sbin/ipmi-sensors",
    "--comma-separated-output",
    "--no-header-output",
    "--output-sensor-state",
    "--output-sensor-thresholds",
    "--entity-sensor-names",
]
THRESHOLD_TERMS = (
    ("lower non-recoverable", "lnr"),
    ("upper non-recoverable", "unr"),
    ("lower critical", "lcr"),
    ("upper critical", "ucr"),
    ("lower non-critical", "lnc"),
    ("upper non-critical", "unc"),
)


def clean(value):
    return value.strip().strip("'").strip()


def number(value):
    text = clean(value)
    if not text or text.upper() in {"N/A", "NA", "UNKNOWN"}:
        return None
    try:
        parsed = float(text)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return parsed if math.isfinite(parsed) else None


def asserted_code(sensor_event):
    lowered = sensor_event.lower()
    for phrase, code in THRESHOLD_TERMS:
        if phrase in lowered:
            return code
    return "none" if lowered in {"", "ok", "n/a", "na"} else "unknown"


def emit(status, **fields):
    event = {
        "collector_schema": 1,
        "collector_status": status,
        "sample_epoch": int(time.time()),
        "bmc_id": platform.node(),
        "collector_tool": "freeipmi-ipmi-sensors",
    }
    event.update(fields)
    print(json.dumps(event, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True), flush=True)


environment = os.environ.copy()
environment.update({"LC_ALL": "C", "LANG": "C"})
try:
    result = subprocess.run(
        COMMAND,
        check=False,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=45,
        env=environment,
    )
except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as error:
    emit("command_error", error_type=type(error).__name__)
    raise SystemExit(0)

if result.returncode != 0:
    emit("command_error", command_returncode=result.returncode)
    raise SystemExit(0)

for row_number, row in enumerate(csv.reader(result.stdout.splitlines()), start=1):
    if len(row) != 13:
        emit("parse_error", row_number=row_number, observed_columns=len(row))
        continue
    record_id, name, sensor_type, tool_state, raw_reading, unit, raw_lnr, raw_lcr, raw_lnc, raw_unc, raw_ucr, raw_unr, sensor_event = map(clean, row)
    thresholds = {
        "threshold_lnr": number(raw_lnr),
        "threshold_lcr": number(raw_lcr),
        "threshold_lnc": number(raw_lnc),
        "threshold_unc": number(raw_unc),
        "threshold_ucr": number(raw_ucr),
        "threshold_unr": number(raw_unr),
    }
    reading = number(raw_reading)
    asserted = asserted_code(sensor_event)
    if any(value is not None for value in thresholds.values()) or asserted not in {"none", "unknown"}:
        event_class = "threshold"
    elif reading is None and sensor_event.lower() not in {"", "ok", "n/a", "na", "unknown"}:
        event_class = "discrete"
    else:
        event_class = "unknown"
    emit(
        "ok",
        sensor_record_id=record_id,
        sensor_name=name,
        sensor_type=sensor_type,
        event_reading_class=event_class,
        reading_valid=1 if reading is not None else 0,
        reading=reading,
        unit=unit or None,
        asserted_threshold=asserted,
        sensor_event=sensor_event,
        active_states=sensor_event if event_class == "discrete" else None,
        tool_state=tool_state.lower(),
        **thresholds,
    )
